question: Invasive predators such as cats, rats and stoats helped cause what share of modern bird, mammal and reptile extinctions?
answer: About three in five. Doherty and colleagues found invasive mammal predators implicated in 142 recorded extinctions of birds, mammals and reptiles, 58% of the total. Cats alone featured in 63. Most were on islands, where animals evolved without such hunters and often nested on the ground. A few ship rats can undo a species.
move: On an island, the newcomer that eats eggs outweighs almost any other threat.
trap: Bulldozers and guns come to mind first, so predators seem a sideshow.
reference: Doherty, Glen, Nimmo, Ritchie & Dickman, Invasive predators and global biodiversity loss, Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 2016
